title: Staged capacity buffering with rollout gates for LTS upgrades
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a conservative, tenant-aware buffering layer and gate-driven rollout process for LTS channel upgrades on dedicated GPU pools. The buffering layer (capacity buffer) temporarily reserves a configurable percentage of pool slots during upgrade waves to absorb tenant bursts and autoscaler churn, reducing forced preemption and long tail latency during drains. This ticket covers: design, rollout gate definitions, autoscaler handshake protocol changes, runbook updates, and observability additions.

Background: Past upgrades caused transient capacity pressure when multiple tenants ramped, leading to elevated evictions and request retries. Existing drain and autoscaler contracts are effective but assume uniform demand. We need a choreography that: 1) preserves SLOs for active tenants, 2) minimizes upgrade duration, 3) respects committed capacity for reserved pools.

Scope:
- Define and implement a capacity-buffer controller that:
  * Allocates a rolling buffer (percent or absolute slots) per pool and per LTS wave.
  * Exposes a safe-zone flag to the autoscaler and admission controller.
- Introduce rollout gates at three levels: preflight (canary health checks), midwave (telemetry-based delay), and final (traffic cutover).
- Extend autoscaler handshake to honor buffer reservations and to coordinate scale-down windows with drain windows.
- Add metrics/dashboards (buffer utilization, failed admission due to buffer, midwave hold count).
- Update upgrade runbook and automated rollback criteria to include buffer saturation thresholds and degradation tolerances.

Non-goals: negotiating cross-cluster tenant migrations, changing existing tenant QoS tiers, or modifying billing behavior at this stage.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity-buffer controller implemented and enabled behind feature flag for dedicated pools.
Autoscaler respects buffer: no scale-down that violates reserved slots during active upgrade waves.
Rollout gates implemented: preflight health checks, midwave telemetry gate, final cutover gate.
Dashboards show buffer utilization, buffer-driven admissions, and gate hold reasons within Console.
Upgrade runbook updated with clear rollback criteria tied to buffer hit-rate and 95th pct latency anomalies.
Integration tests simulate tenant burst and validate <1% increase in evictions versus baseline and no SLO breach for P0 tenants.
implementation_steps: Design API for capacity-buffer controller and define CRD/Config schema (percent/absolute/ttl).
Prototype controller: reserve slots within pool allocator and expose 'safe-zone' to admission layer.
Add autoscaler handshake changes: pre-scale-down check against buffer and a grace-window flag for drains.
Instrument metrics and create Console dashboards and alerts (buffer_saturation, buffer_blocked_admissions, gate_hold_count).
Build rollout gate evaluator service: hooks for canary checks, telemetry thresholds, and manual override endpoints.
Create end-to-end test harness: synthetic tenants, burst profiles, and automated validation of rollback triggers.
Dogfood on staging dedicated cluster with controlled waves; run checklist and iterate on thresholds.
Gradual enablement via feature flag: 10% pools -> 33% -> 100% with post-wave reviews.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: RFC posted to #eng-release; initial design validated by SRE and Platform. Decision: buffer default 6% or min 2 slots, configurable per pool.
2026-02-17: Prototype capacity-buffer CRD implemented; basic admission integration complete. Observability stubbed in Prometheus.
2026-02-19: Autoscaler handshake design reviewed. Trade-off: longer drain grace reduces eviction but extends upgrade time; set default grace-window to 90s with per-pool tuning.
2026-02-20: Integration tests added to CI; staging rollout scheduled for 2026-02-25 behind feature flag 'buffered-upgrades'.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-reserving capacity could reduce effective throughput and increase customer latency during normal operations. Mitigation: conservative defaults, telemetry-driven auto-release of unused buffer after TTL, and ability to emergency disable buffer per pool. Risk: complex autoscaler interactions causing oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis and rate-limit scale decisions during active waves.
